name: banner
title: App banner
what: One shared header every adopting app links: page navigation (strip or sidebar) the person can arrange for themselves (hide pages from the sidebar, pin, reorder, a home page), the person's preferences everywhere or per app, their apps with stars, one drawer from the avatar, info bubbles, a derived tour and read-me, and People and Permissions over the data-access-url contract.

attributes.data-app-name: the app's name as people say it
attributes.data-version: the app's version; printed with exactly one leading v
attributes.data-mark: an image URL for the app's mark (default: its initials)
attributes.data-profile-url: the person's preferences route (default {hub}/api/profile; empty = this browser only)
attributes.data-avatar: an app-supplied picture that wins over the person's mark
attributes.data-role: their role here; 'admin' in it shows the Admins-only section, 'super admin' the View-as card
attributes.data-access-url: the People and Permissions contract endpoint
attributes.data-readme-url: an authored read-me: {lead, sections:[{head, lines}], note}
attributes.data-theme-external: present when the app owns <html data-theme> itself
attributes.data-fixes-url: the app's own gated re-serve of /hub/app-fixes.json?app=<slug> ({fixes, metadata, etag}), passing If-None-Match / X-Hub-ETag through and 304 back. Turns on the Fixes button: every error this app forwarded that reached the board, the board task it became, the fixer's steps live, and a notice when one is reported and when it is fixed (the first read is a baseline and raises none). Polled every 8 s while a fix is open, 45 s otherwise, never while the tab is hidden.

islands.nav: [{label, href, icon, hint, sep, current, count, countId, children:[...]}]
islands.profile: [{label, href | id, icon, sub, info}] -- the app's own rows for the person
islands.admin: [{label, href | id, icon, sub, info}] -- admin-only rows
islands.help: [{label, href | id, icon, sub, info}] -- extra How-this-works rows

mount.slot: [data-ab-slot] -- the app's own controls, left of the band's

storage: localStorage ab:prefs (a cache of the person's record, including nav_hidden and nav_layout)
localStorage ab:fixes:<app> (which fix notices this browser has already shown)
html_attributes: data-ab-strip (on the mount: the strip look from the `strip` property)

rules: The person's arrangement is theirs, in this app: pages hidden from the sidebar (nav_hidden) and pinned, reordered and home (nav_layout) live on their hub record as their own per-app maps, never inside the per-app display overrides, so 'use my everywhere-settings here' does not undo them.

Row keys are a page's label, or 'Group / Page' for a sub-page, compared only against the pages the app declares now: a renamed page comes back where the app put it. The failure direction is shown, never lost.

Hiding is the sidebar's: the strip has no foot for the way back and draws every page. The page you are on is never concealed; a group whose every page is hidden goes with them; 'Show N hidden' at the sidebar's foot is the way back and exists only while something is hidden.

The home page drives the band's name link; arriving at the app's root from outside the app, in the first moments of the page, with no query or fragment, and only when data-home is absolute, lands there.
A redraw never rearranges: the navigation is rebuilt only when what it is drawn from changed, and a rebuilt sidebar keeps each group's open state and its scroll.
One profile save in the air at a time: a change made meanwhile is queued and sent after it, in order, and the answer to a save that has been overtaken is not adopted.
A menu opened by hover gives no focus back when it closes; one opened by a click or the keyboard does.

props.label: Page strip look
props.hint: How the page strip under the band marks the page you point at and the page you are on. Classic is the earlier look, kept one setting away.

options.label: Underline: a line grows under the page you point at; the current page keeps it in the accent
Classic: a ground behind the page you point at; a bottom border under the current page
